protocol.description:
This protocol allows the river-window-management-v1 window manager to draw scaled and translucent mirrors of windows, for window animations and overviews.
A mirror shows the buffers of a window without copying them. The compositor animates mirrors itself, at the refresh rate of the outputs, so animations stay smooth regardless of how fast the window manager responds.
Mirrors are drawn above all windows and below the top layer of the layer shell, in the order they were created, and never receive input.
Note: this is a downstream extension maintained with the Pangolin desktop, it is not part of upstream river.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.

interface.name: river_window_effects_v1
interface.description: This global interface should only be advertised to the client if the river_window_manager_v1 global is also advertised.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the river_window_effects_v1 object. Existing mirrors are not affected.

request.name: get_mirror
request.description:
Create a mirror of the window. The mirror follows the content of the window until the window is destroyed or the mirror is frozen. While a mirror is visible, the compositor keeps sending frame callbacks to the window as if it was visible, even if it is hidden.
The mirror starts out at the current position and size of the window, fully transparent.
If the window is inert the mirror is empty.

request.name: set_closing_mirrors

description.summary: get a mirror of each window that closes

request.description: If enabled is non-zero, the compositor sends a closing_mirror event for every window of the window manager that is unmapped, so that the window manager can animate it away. Disabled by default.

event.name: closing_mirror
event.description:
The window is being unmapped. The new mirror shows its last content, it starts out at the position and size the window was rendered at, fully transparent.
The event is sent before the river_window_v1.closed event, while the window is still rendered: making the mirror visible before finishing the manage sequence in which the window is closed avoids a gap.

interface.name: river_window_mirror_v1
interface.description: The geometry of a mirror maps the geometry of the window (as reported by river_window_v1.dimensions) to a rectangle in the compositor's logical coordinate space. Parts of the window outside its geometry, such as client side shadows, are scaled the same way.

request.name: destroy
request.description: The mirror stops being drawn immediately.

request.name: freeze
request.description: Keep the current content of the window and stop following it.

request.name: animate

description.summary: animate the mirror to a new state

request.description:
Animate from the current state of the mirror to the given position, size and opacity over duration milliseconds, following the CSS style cubic bezier timing curve (0,0) (x1,y1) (x2,y2) (1,1). A duration of 0 applies the new state immediately.
A new animation replaces the current one, starting from the state the mirror is drawn at.

event.name: done
event.description: Sent when an animation with a non-zero duration completes without being replaced by another one.
